title.es: Enlaces, elisiones y acento de frase

es: Predecir cómo se enlazan y se omiten sonidos entre palabras (next day, old man, turn it off) y completar frases dictadas con la forma realmente pronunciada.

teaching.en: When people talk fast, they blend words, so 'pick it up' sounds like one word.
teaching.es: Cuando la gente habla rápido, une las palabras, y «pick it up» suena como una sola palabra.
teaching.explanationEs: Pick it up se oye «pi-ki-tup»: las palabras se funden.
segments: When people talk fast, they blend words, so
'pick it up' sounds like one word.
teaching.audioText: When people talk fast, they blend words, so 'pick it up' sounds like one word.

teaching.en: A final consonant joins the next vowel: 'turn it off' sounds like 'tur-ni-toff'.
teaching.es: Una consonante final se une a la vocal siguiente: «turn it off» suena «tur-ni-toff».
teaching.explanationEs: La n de turn y la t de it pasan a empezar la sílaba siguiente.
segments: A final consonant joins the next vowel:
teaching.audioText: A final consonant joins the next vowel: 'turn it off' sounds like 'tur-ni-toff'.

teaching.en: Many speakers drop the t in 'next day', so you hear 'nex day'.
teaching.es: Muchos hablantes omiten la t de «next day», y se oye «nex day».
teaching.explanationEs: La t casi desaparece entre dos consonantes, pero se escribe.
segments: Many speakers drop the t in 'next
teaching.audioText: Many speakers drop the t in 'next day', so you hear 'nex day'.

teaching.en: We swallow the d in 'old man', and it sounds like 'ol man'.
teaching.es: Nos tragamos la d de «old man», y suena «ol man».
teaching.explanationEs: La d entre dos consonantes se debilita mucho.
segments: We swallow the d in 'old man',
teaching.audioText: We swallow the d in 'old man', and it sounds like 'ol man'.

teaching.explanationEs: Las palabras importantes se pronuncian más fuerte y largas.
teaching.audioText: In 'I can't find my keys', the stressed word is 'keys'.

teaching.en: You link 'last' and 'night' in fast speech, and the t almost disappears.
teaching.es: Enlazas «last» y «night» al hablar rápido, y la t casi desaparece.
teaching.explanationEs: Al enlazar dos palabras, la consonante débil se pierde.
segments: speech, and the t almost disappears.
teaching.audioText: You link 'last' and 'night' in fast speech, and the t almost disappears.

teaching.en: Weak words like 'to' and 'the' are quick, so the rhythm comes from the stressed words.
